after: ## Measuring a length with a ruler
alt: An object is measured from the 1.0 cm mark to the 4.4 cm mark, giving 3.4 cm, as a way round a worn zero end. An eye looking straight down at the scale reads correctly while one looking from the side gives a parallax error. A ball's diameter is the gap between two blocks placed against it at right angles to the ruler.
caption: Subtract the start reading, look straight down, and use blocks for round objects.

after: ## Measuring a volume with a measuring cylinder
alt: Left: a measuring cylinder on a level bench, read with the eye level with the bottom of the curved meniscus. Right: 18 cm³ of water in a 25 cm³ cylinder marked every 0.5 cm³ and in a 250 cm³ cylinder marked every 5 cm³; the smaller cylinder gives the more precise reading.
caption: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level, in the smallest suitable cylinder.

alt: Three examples of measuring multiples. A stack of 20 coins is 37.0 mm tall, so one coin is 1.85 mm thick. Thirty touching turns of wire on a pencil span 12.0 mm, so the wire is 0.40 mm across. Timing from drip "zero" to the tenth drip gives 6.5 s for 10 intervals, or 0.65 s each.
caption: Dividing a multiple shares the measuring uncertainty between all the items.

alt: A pendulum swinging between two positions either side of a fiducial mark below its centre. One oscillation is a swing across and back again. Release the bob a small distance to one side, start timing as it passes the mark counting "zero", count passes in the same direction, time 20 oscillations, repeat, and divide the mean time by 20.
caption: Time many oscillations from the centre mark, then divide.

alt: Left: a boat heading across a river at 3.0 m/s with a 1.2 m/s current has a resultant velocity of 3.2 m/s at 22° downstream from straight across. Right: forces of 600 N east and 450 N north drawn tip to tail at 1 cm to 100 N give a 7.5 cm resultant, 750 N at 37° north of east.
caption: Draw the vectors tip to tail; use Pythagoras and tan θ, and always state the reference direction.
